keyPhrases.text: Pfeiffer has no trouble with that song
She can reach way into her upper register with stores of vocal power
using something originally written for the stage as a model is a good idea
the presiding emotional affect ends up being melancholy
The new songs are, well, fine
sit in awkward tension against jukebox classics
make the new songs sound inferior

reasoning: Mixed review with both appreciation and significant reservations. Acknowledges strong vocal performances and some effective moments, but criticizes the show as derivative ('memory of a memory'), notes awkward integration of new vs. classic songs, and describes the overall effect as melancholy rather than triumphant. The tone is more analytical than enthusiastic, placing it in the mixed-positive range.
